title: Eating out with friends
goal: Order street food and restaurant meals for a group, say a dish is too spicy or needs salt, say what you feel like eating, and sort out the bill: a treat, split, or packed to take away.
intro:
Food is how friends meet in Maharashtra: vada pav and cutting chai at the station, a fiery **मिसळ** on a Sunday morning in Pune, pav bhaji on the beach in Mumbai, a big **थाळी** when someone's family is in town.

This unit gives you the street-stall and restaurant lines — **काय मागवायचं?**, **हे जरा जास्तच तिखट आहे!**, **पुरे, पुरे!**, **आज माझ्याकडून!** — and two pieces of grammar: how to say **too, enough and a little** (जास्तच, पुरेसा, थोडा), and the lovely Marathi way to say **'I feel like…'**: **मला काहीतरी गोड खावंसं वाटतंय**.

grammar.title: Too, enough, a little: जास्तच, पुरेसा, थोडा
grammar.body:
**Too (much).** Marathi has no separate word for 'too'. Use **जास्त** 'more, too much', made stronger with **-च**: **जरा जास्तच तिखट** 'a bit too spicy'. **फार** means 'very' and, with a complaint, 'too': चहा **फार** गोड आहे 'the tea's too sweet'. **खूप** is 'very, a lot'.

**Not enough.** Say the thing is **कमी** 'less': **मीठ कमी आहे** 'it needs salt', **तिखट कमी आहे** 'it's not spicy enough'. Marathi even has one word for 'not salty enough': **अळणी**; too salty is **खारट**.

**Enough.** **पुरे!** 'enough!' (also **बस!**); the adjective **पुरेसा** 'sufficient' agrees with the thing: भात **पुरेसा** (m), भाजी **पुरेशी** (f), पाणी **पुरेसं** (n), दोन प्लेट **पुरेशा** (f pl).

**A little, more.** **थोडा / थोडी / थोडं** 'a little' agree too; **जरा** 'a bit' never changes. **आणखी** or **अजून** 'more': आणखी एक प्लेट.

The trap: **कमी तिखट** before the dish or verb is a request ('make it less spicy'), but **तिखट कमी आहे** is a complaint ('not spicy enough').

grammar.title: I feel like…: खावंसं वाटतं
grammar.body:
To say you feel like doing something, Marathi uses **वाटणे** 'to feel' with the person in **-ला** and a special form of the verb: the 'should' form you know from unit 9 (**खावं, प्यावं, जावं, करावं**) plus **-सं**:

**मला** काहीतरी गोड **खावंसं वाटतंय** 'I feel like something sweet' (lit. 'to me it seems worth eating something sweet').

**Forms:** खा → **खावंसं**, पी → **प्यावंसं**, जा → **जावंसं**, कर → **करावंसं**, बघ → **बघावंसं**, झोप → **झोपावंसं**.

**Agreement.** With a stated object, careful speech makes both words agree with it: **चहा प्यावासा वाटतोय** (m), **कॉफी प्यावीशी वाटतेय** (f), **पाणी प्यावंसं वाटतंय** (n). With no object, or with काहीतरी / काहीच, it's the neuter **-वंसं वाटतं**, and in casual speech many people use the neuter for everything.

**Tense** is on वाटणे: **वाटतंय** (right now), **वाटतं** (in general), **वाटलं** (felt), **वाटत नाहीये** (don't feel like it now).

The trap: the person takes **-ला**, not मी: **मला** जावंसं वाटतं, never *मी जावंसं वाटतो*.

dialogue.title: Sunday misal
dialogue.setting: Pune, Sunday morning at a crowded misal place in Sadashiv Peth. Rohit, Anjali and Sameer, old college friends, have queued for twenty minutes.

culture: Every Marathi city argues about food. Pune's Sunday ritual is **मिसळ** — a sprouted-bean curry topped with farsan and a layer of red, oily **तर्री** — eaten with pav and a cutting chai, often after a queue; Kolhapur's version is even hotter. Mumbai runs on **वडापाव** from station stalls, pav bhaji and bhel on the beach, and the bun-maska and chai of the old **Irani cafés**. Pune's **मस्तानी** is a thick milkshake topped with ice cream. In a home or at a thali restaurant, the server keeps refilling your plate (this hospitable pressing is called **आग्रह**): say **पुरे, पुरे!** or cover the plate with your hand, and expect to be told **घ्या हो, थोडं तरी!** 'go on, just a little!' Among friends, whoever has news — a salary, a new job, a birthday — is expected to pay: **आज माझ्याकडून** or the friends will demand **पार्टी!**; otherwise people split the bill and settle it by UPI on the spot. Tips are small and not compulsory, and you call the waiter **दादा**, **भाऊ** or **काका**, not 'waiter'.

tip.title: Ordering at a stall, and praising it
tip.body:
- Name it and the number: **दोन वडापाव, एक कटिंग**; put **भाऊ / दादा** in front.
- **प्लेट** counts portions: **एक प्लेट पाणीपुरी**; **आणखी एक** 'one more'.
- Praise it with **मस्त झालंय!** — the verb agrees with the dish: वडापाव मस्त **झालाय** (m), भेळ मस्त **झालीये** (f).

tip.title: For me, for her: -साठी
tip.body:
- 'For' is **-साठी** on the oblique: **माझ्यासाठी** 'for me', **तिच्यासाठी** 'for her', **सगळ्यांसाठी** 'for everyone'.
- Ask staff politely with the **-आ** form + ना: **मेन्यू दाखवा ना**, **ऑर्डर घ्या ना**.
- 'Shall we order…?' = **मागवूया का?**; 'what shall we order?' = **काय मागवायचं?**

tip.title: Too, enough: जास्तच, कमी, पुरेसा
tip.body:
- Too: **जरा जास्तच** + adjective, or **फार**: चहा फार गोड आहे.
- Not enough: **X कमी आहे**: मीठ कमी आहे. One word for 'needs salt': **अळणी**.
- Enough: **पुरे!**; the adjective **पुरेसा / पुरेशी / पुरेसं** agrees with the thing.
tip.pattern: जरा जास्तच + adj · X कमी आहे · X पुरेसा आहे

tip.title: मला … खावंसं वाटतंय — I feel like…
tip.body:
- Person + **-ला**, then the 'should' form + **सं**, then **वाटणे**: मला **खावंसं वाटतंय**.
- खा → **खावंसं**, पी → **प्यावंसं**, जा → **जावंसं**, कर → **करावंसं**, झोप → **झोपावंसं**.
- Not right now: **वाटत नाहीये**. In general: **वाटतं**.
- Never *मी खावंसं वाटतो* — it's **मला**.

tip.title: Who pays?
tip.body:
- Treating: **आज माझ्याकडून!** 'today's on me' (lit. from me); someone else's turn: **तुझ्याकडून**.
- Splitting: **बिल वाटून घेऊया**; **प्रत्येकी** 'each'.
- Refusing their money: **राहू दे!** 'leave it!'
- Takeaway: **पॅक करा** (or पार्सल करा).
